rv.q: The striking thing about this excellent revival is how little this witty, wintry kitchen-sink drama has aged.
One of the best choices Sheibani has made is to avoid turning the play into a hysterical screechfest.
Bijan Sheibani's production is faithful to Delaney's text and although some of the topics no longer feel shocking, they continue to resonate.

Admidst the Formica tables and shabby gas cooker, a three piece onstage band unobtrusively lends backing for the few musical blues/jazz numbers which occasionally punctuate the scenes and serve to lift the whole production well above its humble origins.
A Taste of Honey is well worth tasting.

cn.t: Sheibani's faithful revival proves Delaney's 1958 working-class drama hasn't aged, with its taboo subjects still resonating today. Critics praise the witty writing and strong performances, particularly avoiding melodrama in this excellent National Theatre transfer.
